Also, do you have any underlying health conditions like diabetes or issues with your circulation?

speaker: Doctor
text:
The test results are reassuring; your glucose, blood counts, and wound culture are all normal, suggesting this isn't an acute infection or typical diabetic ulcer. Given the chronic nature of the wound on your right lower leg, do you notice any changes in color, swelling, or pain around the area? Also, have you ever had your varicose veins or circulation issues evaluated?

REQUEST IMAGES: Right lower leg wound and vascular ultrasound.

speaker: Patient
text: 57-year-old male. The patient reports a large wound on his right lower leg that has been present for 6 months. He mentions that his legs have been chronically swollen for over 10 years and that his mother and brother had similar leg problems. He had a documented deep vein thrombosis (DVT) in the affected leg 5 years ago but has no other significant past medical history.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Given your history of DVT, long-standing bilateral leg swelling, and family history, this clinical picture strongly suggests a venous etiology. Can you describe if the wound edges are irregular or rolled, and do you experience heaviness or aching that worsens by the end of the day?

DIAGNOSIS READY: Venous Stasis Ulcer secondary to chronic venous insufficiency and prior DVT.
